1.modern-en: Lear announces his plan to divide the kingdom, stages the love test, disowns Cordelia for refusing to flatter him, and banishes Kent for objecting.

4.modern-en: Lear arrives at Goneril's palace with his hundred knights, is met with insolence by Goneril and Oswald, and curses her with barrenness.

5.modern-en: Lear leaves Goneril's for Regan's, already half-aware he has made a terrible mistake, but unwilling to say so.

9.modern-en: Lear arrives at Gloucester's castle to find Kent in the stocks, is met coldly by Regan and Goneril, and storms out into the gathering storm rather than reduce his retinue.

11.modern-en: Lear rages on the heath in the full storm, calling on the elements to crack their cheeks and split the world open.

13.modern-en: Lear meets the disguised Edgar as Poor Tom at the hovel, strips off his clothes, and pronounces him a philosopher.

15.modern-en: Lear in the farmhouse puts his daughters on imaginary trial, with the Fool and Poor Tom as his fellow judges.

20.modern-en: Lear, recovered enough to know his daughter, kneels to Cordelia at the French camp and asks her forgiveness.

23.modern-en: Lear is taken prisoner with Cordelia after the battle and tells her happily that they will sing together in their cage.

24.modern-en: Lear enters carrying the body of the hanged Cordelia, asks the gods why a dog should live and she have no breath, and dies of grief looking at her lips.

1.modern-en: Cordelia refuses to take part in the love contest and is disinherited; the King of France takes her without a dowry.

19.modern-en: Cordelia is reported to have landed in Britain with a French army, weeping over the news of her father's treatment.

20.modern-en: Cordelia tends Lear in the French camp, has him brought in dressed in fresh clothes, and is recognised by him.

23.modern-en: Cordelia is taken prisoner with Lear after the battle and asks calmly to see her sisters.

24.modern-en: Cordelia is hanged in prison on Edmund's orders and is carried in dead in her father's arms.

epithet.en: Lear's eldest daughter, Duchess of Albany

1.modern-en: Goneril delivers the first prize-winning speech of devotion to Lear and inherits the largest portion of the kingdom.

4.modern-en: Goneril complains to Oswald of her father's knights, tells Lear to reduce his retinue, and provokes him into walking out.

5.modern-en: Goneril is mentioned in the brief journey to Regan's; the sisters' alliance is already forming.

14.modern-en: Goneril sends Edmund back to her own court with a love-token while Albany grows increasingly suspicious.

18.modern-en: Goneril quarrels openly with Albany at her palace and is informed that Cornwall has been killed.

26.modern-en: Goneril poisons her sister Regan out of jealousy over Edmund, watches Edmund mortally wounded by Edgar, and kills herself offstage.

epithet.en: Lear's middle daughter, Duchess of Cornwall

1.modern-en: Regan delivers the second love-test speech and inherits her share of the kingdom.

9.modern-en: Regan arrives at Gloucester's castle and joins Goneril in refusing Lear his retinue, then orders the gates shut against him.

16.modern-en: Regan, with her husband Cornwall, helps blind Gloucester in his own house and kills the servant who tries to stop them.

18.modern-en: Regan is widowed by Cornwall's wound and immediately makes a claim on Edmund.

22.modern-en: Regan, riding to the British camp, makes her interest in Edmund explicit to Oswald and to Edmund himself.

26.modern-en: Regan dies on stage from the poison Goneril has given her.

epithet.en: Edgar and Edmund's father, the play's second old man

2.modern-en: Gloucester is shown a forged letter by Edmund and is convinced that Edgar is plotting against him.

6.modern-en: Gloucester finds Edmund 'wounded' by Edgar and orders Edgar pursued through the country.

7.modern-en: Gloucester apologises to Kent for the night's events outside the castle.

9.modern-en: Gloucester pleads with Lear, with Regan, and with Goneril for his old king through the storm scene.

12.modern-en: Gloucester tells Edmund secretly that he intends to help Lear, not knowing Edmund will at once betray the confidence.

14.modern-en: Gloucester is betrayed by Edmund to Cornwall and Regan as a French sympathiser.

16.modern-en: Gloucester is bound to a chair by Cornwall, accused of treason, and blinded in his own hall; he is then thrown out to find his way by smell to Dover.

17.modern-en: Gloucester is led across the heath by the disguised Edgar as Poor Tom and asks to be brought to the cliffs at Dover.

24.modern-en: Gloucester is reported dead of joy and grief after Edgar finally reveals himself to him.

2.modern-en: Edmund opens the bastard's great soliloquy on the gods of bastards, forges the letter against Edgar, and sets the subplot in motion.

6.modern-en: Edmund stages a flesh-wound on himself to convince Gloucester that Edgar attacked him.

14.modern-en: Edmund betrays his father to Cornwall and Regan with a forged letter from France.

16.modern-en: Edmund is rewarded with his father's title as Earl of Gloucester after the blinding.

18.modern-en: Edmund is courted by both Regan and Goneril after Cornwall's death.

22.modern-en: Edmund commands the British army at Dover and orders Cordelia and Lear quietly killed in prison.

26.modern-en: Edmund is challenged anonymously, defeated in single combat by his brother Edgar, and dies trying to undo the order for Cordelia's death too late.

epithet.en: Gloucester's legitimate son, who disguises himself as Poor Tom

2.modern-en: Edgar is duped by Edmund into the false belief that his father is angry with him.

8.modern-en: Edgar, hunted, resolves to disguise himself as the half-naked mad beggar 'Poor Tom.'

11.modern-en: Edgar as Poor Tom meets Lear's party in the storm and is taken into the hovel.

13.modern-en: Edgar continues his Tom o' Bedlam disguise and Lear declares him a philosopher.

15.modern-en: Edgar joins Lear's mock trial of the daughters in the farmhouse.

17.modern-en: Edgar leads his blinded father across the heath and, at Dover, stages a fall from an imaginary cliff to save him.

20.modern-en: Edgar still in disguise hands Goneril's love letter to Albany after killing Oswald in the road.

24.modern-en: Edgar reveals himself to his father, who dies of joy.

26.modern-en: Edgar appears as the anonymous challenger at the camp, kills Edmund, and is asked at the close to take up the rule of the kingdom.

epithet.en: A loyal nobleman, later in disguise as Caius

1.modern-en: Kent objects to Lear's disinheritance of Cordelia, is banished, and resolves to return in disguise.

4.modern-en: Kent returns disguised as 'Caius' and is taken into Lear's service as a serving-man.

5.modern-en: Kent rides ahead with letters to Regan and Cornwall.

6.modern-en: Kent confronts Oswald outside Gloucester's castle and beats him soundly.

7.modern-en: Kent is put in the stocks by Cornwall as the play's first explicit insult to the king's man.

9.modern-en: Kent is in the stocks when Lear arrives at Gloucester's castle, sparking Lear's first rage.

10.modern-en: Kent meets a Gentleman on the heath and arranges to send word to Cordelia in France.

11.modern-en: Kent guides Lear through the storm and finds them shelter at the hovel.

13.modern-en: Kent leads the others into the hovel and tries to keep Lear from injuring himself.

15.modern-en: Kent endures the mock trial in the farmhouse and helps carry Lear off when he finally sleeps.

17.modern-en: Kent reports to a Gentleman at Dover that Cordelia has read his news and is moved.

22.modern-en: Kent in disguise continues to attend Lear in the French camp.

26.modern-en: Kent reveals himself to Lear at the very end and declines the kingdom Albany would share, hinting he means to die after his master.

4.modern-en: The Fool joins Lear at Goneril's palace and tells him, in song and riddle, that he gave the rod to his daughters and put down his own breeches.

5.modern-en: The Fool jokes about the kingdom Lear has given away on the road from Goneril's to Regan's.

9.modern-en: The Fool follows Lear out of Gloucester's castle into the storm.

11.modern-en: The Fool keeps up his bitter jokes through the storm, urging Lear to ask his daughters' blessing instead.

13.modern-en: The Fool helps coax Lear into the hovel and is frightened by Poor Tom.

15.modern-en: The Fool joins the mock trial in the farmhouse and disappears from the play with the line 'I'll go to bed at noon.'

epithet.en: Goneril's husband, a slow-to-act good man

1.modern-en: Albany is at the love-test ceremony as Goneril's husband but says nothing through it.

3.modern-en: Albany is mentioned in Goneril's house as the husband she finds too soft.

4.modern-en: Albany comes in late to Goneril's quarrel with Lear and tries to calm her, half-aware of what is wrong.

18.modern-en: Albany finally breaks with Goneril when he hears of Gloucester's blinding and Cornwall's death.

26.modern-en: Albany presides over the closing scene, condemns Edmund, and offers the kingdom jointly to Kent and Edgar.

epithet.en: Regan's husband, the play's primary onstage villain

6.modern-en: Cornwall is mentioned as the duke Regan has gone to with her sister's letters.

7.modern-en: Cornwall orders Kent placed in the stocks against Gloucester's protests.

9.modern-en: Cornwall closes his gates against Lear in the storm.

12.modern-en: Cornwall summons Gloucester back to the castle once Edmund has betrayed him.

14.modern-en: Cornwall sends out a hunt for Edgar and confirms Edmund as the new Earl of Gloucester.

16.modern-en: Cornwall blinds Gloucester in his own hall and is mortally wounded by a servant who cannot bear to watch.
